<scalar-card title="arena" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#arena">

<scalar-card title="ctEq" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#cteq">

<scalar-card title="ctSelect" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#ctselect">

<scalar-card title="f64ToBits" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#f64tobits">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="geteuid" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#geteuid">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="isDirectorySync" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#isdirectorysync">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="isExecutableSync" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#isexecutablesync">

<scalar-card title="kill" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#kill">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="lstatOwnerModeSync" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#lstatownermodesync">

One `lstat` of `path`, so a symbolic link answers for itself: the owner's uid in the high 32 bits and `st_mode` in the low 32, or -1 when the path does not resolve (#386).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="mkdirSync" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#mkdirsync">

One directory, not recursive; whether a directory is there afterwards.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="mkdirSyncMode" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#mkdirsyncmode">

One directory made with `mode` less the umask (`0o700` is exact under any umask that leaves the owner's bits): 0, or a negative errno.

<scalar-card title="monotonicNanos" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#monotonicnanos">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="netAddress" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#netaddress">

Write the address form of a numeric `host` and `port` into `out`: 0, or -22.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="netClose" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#netclose">

Close the descriptor.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="netLocalPort" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#netlocalport">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="netMss" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#netmss">

A connected TCP socket's send MSS, the payload bytes one segment carries; -1, never an errno, for anything else, and always on wasm.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="netRead" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#netread">

Up to `len` bytes into `buf` from `off`: the count, 0 at end of stream, or -11.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="netSetOption" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#netsetoption">

Set one socket option from a whitelist: `option` is one of the `NET_*` ids below, and any other is -22; there is no raw level and option number. 0, or a negative errno (-9 a closed descriptor, -88 not a socket).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="netShutdown" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#netshutdown">

Shut the read side (0), the write side (1) or both (2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="netWrite" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#netwrite">

<scalar-card title="netWrite2" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#netwrite2">

`netWrite` of `a`'s range then `b`'s, in one system call: the count of both, at most `aLen + bLen`.

<scalar-card title="panic" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#panic">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="pollWait" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#pollwait">

<scalar-card title="readCString" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#readcstring">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="readFileBytesSync" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#readfilebytessync">

The file's bytes as they are on disk — no UTF-8 assumed, so a zero byte and a byte of 0x80 or above survive — or `null` for every path `readFileSyncOrNull` answers `null` for.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="readFileSync" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#readfilesync">

The whole file as a string; a path that cannot be read as one — missing, a directory, a parent that cannot be searched — prints `nish: cannot read <path>` and exits 1.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="readFileSyncOrNull" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#readfilesyncornull">

The same read, answering `null` for every path the other exits over.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="readSignal" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#readsignal">

Block until SIGTERM or SIGINT arrives and answer its number, 15 or 2; -1 for any `fd` that is not `signalFd()`'s.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="readStdin" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#readstdin">

Up to `len` bytes of stdin into `buf` from `off`, never blocking: the count, 0 at end of stream, or -11 when nothing is waiting.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="readdirSync" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#readdirsync">

The directory's entries, sorted ascending by bytes and without `.` or `..`, or `null` when it cannot be read.

<scalar-card title="realpathSync" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#realpathsync">

<scalar-card title="recvFd" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#recvfd">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="renameSync" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#renamesync">

`from` moved to `to`, replacing a file there in one step on one file system: 0, or a negative errno (-18 across file systems, -2 for a missing `from`).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="secureZero" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#securezero">

Every byte of `bytes` set to zero, in stores neither `-O2` nor `-flto` may drop as dead (#385): how a key, a secret scalar or another secret is cleared once it is used.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="sendFd" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#sendfd">

Send `buf[off..off+len)` over the Unix socket `sock` with a copy of the descriptor `fd` (`SCM_RIGHTS`): the bytes sent, or a negative errno; -22 a zero `len` or a negative `fd`, -9 a closed `sock` or `fd`, -88 a `sock` that is not a socket, -95 one that is not Unix.

<scalar-card title="setIdlePriority" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#setidlepriority">

Move this process to `SCHED_IDLE`, which runs it only when nothing else wants the CPU: 0, or a negative errno, and -95 where the host has no such policy (Darwin).

<scalar-card title="setNice" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#setnice">

<scalar-card title="setRawMode" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#setrawmode">

<scalar-card title="setTerminalRestore" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#setterminalrestore">

Bytes the runtime writes to the terminal on stdout at exit, on a panic and on every signal that ends the program (SIGKILL aside), before termios is restored.

A descriptor that becomes readable when SIGTERM or SIGINT arrives, whichever thread the signal lands on, made once (every call answers the same one), or -1.

<scalar-card title="spawn" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#spawn">

<scalar-card title="spawnPiped" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#spawnpiped">

The same run with all three streams on pipes: `stdin` is written to the child and closed, and what it prints is appended to `stdout` and `stderr`.

<scalar-card title="spawnSync" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#spawnsync">

<scalar-card title="spawnSyncTo" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#spawnsyncto">

<scalar-card title="spawnWithFds" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#spawnwithfds">

The modification time of `path` in milliseconds since the epoch, with the sub-millisecond fraction the file system keeps (Node's `mtimeMs`), or NaN when it cannot be stat'd.

<scalar-card title="tcpListenFlags" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tcplistenflags">

<scalar-callout type="info">

Every Nish program is legal TypeScript syntax — the compiler parses it
with the official TypeScript parser and nothing else. This file is what
makes it legal TypeScript *semantics* too: reference it from a `tsconfig.json`
(or with `/// <reference path="..." />`) and `tsc --noEmit`, your editor and
your language server all accept `Result<T, E>`, `Ok(...)`, `i32` and the rest
without a red squiggle.

```text
{ "include": ["src/**/*.ts", "node_modules/nish/runtime/nish.d.ts"] }
```

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="nish is still the authority">

TypeScript's structural checker is
weaker than this compiler's in the places where Nish is deliberately
stricter, and it cannot see the flow rules at all:

- the integer and float widths are aliases of `number` here, so `tsc`
  lets an `i32` and an `f64` mix where `nish` refuses;
- `tsc` does not know that a `Result` may not be dropped, that
  `orReturn()` returns early, or that the enclosing function has to
  return a `Result` of its own for it to be legal at all;
- everything Phase 0 forbids (`any`, `throw`, `try`, prototypes,
  arrow functions, ...) is ordinary TypeScript and passes `tsc` happily.

</scalar-detail>

So a program that `tsc` accepts may still be rejected by `nish`; the
reverse should never happen, and a case where it does is a bug in this file.
`docs/LANGUAGE.md` is the normative description.

<scalar-detail title="Map and Set are not declared here">

**`Map` and `Set` are not declared here**, although `nish` has them as
globals: the `"lib": ["ES2022"]` a program is checked against already
declares JavaScript's, and a second declaration would clash with it.
`nish`'s are that surface less what it defers — no `entries`, no `forEach`,
no `for...of` over a `Map` itself — with `keys()` and `values()` admitted
only as the iterable of a `for...of`, and `get`'s `V | undefined` only as a
`const`'s initialiser, the left of `??` or an operand of `=== undefined`,
none of which `tsc` can know (docs/LANGUAGE.md -> `Map` and `Set`).
`nish/map`'s `reserve` and `getOrInsert` are not declared here either: they
are ordinary source, `std/map.ts`, which `tsconfig.json` maps `nish/*` to.

</scalar-detail>

## arena

`using a = arena()` (docs/LANGUAGE.md -> Arena): everything the block
allocates after this declaration is released when the block ends, on every
exit, and the compiler refuses the block if anything allocated in it could
outlive it. Only a `using` initialiser, and the binding is never read; under
Node there is no arena and the disposal does nothing.

```ts
function arena(): Disposable
```

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Disposable">
</scalar-field>

## createFileExclusiveSync

`data` in a new file of exactly `mode`, created only if nothing is at `path`:
-17 when something is, a dangling symbolic link included. Of several
processes racing for one path exactly one succeeds, so it takes a lock. The
byte count, or a negative errno; a write that fails after the create
removes the file, so the lock is not left taken. Never an exit.

```ts
function createFileExclusiveSync(
  path: string,
  data: string,
  mode: i32,
): i32
```

`writeFileSync` with an explicit `mode`: the file is exactly `mode`
(`0o600` for a secret) before a byte of `data` is in it, whatever the umask
or a file already there had, and a symbolic link at the path is refused
(-40). The byte count, or a negative errno: -22 for a mode outside
0..0o777, the setuid, setgid and sticky bits included. The file is
truncated and written in place, so a crash or a failed write leaves it
empty or partial, and a file this process may write but does not own is
emptied before the mode change answers -1 (`EPERM`). For a file that must
be the old one or the new one, write a temporary name with this and move it
with `renameSync`. Never an exit.

## CPtr

`CPtr` (WP27 S2): the address a `declare function` hands back, opaque and
eight bytes wide. `docs/LANGUAGE.md` has the rules — it may be written in a
`declare function` signature and on a local, compared with `null` or with
another `CPtr`, and passed back to C, and that is all.

An empty interface with a private brand rather than `unknown` or a type
alias: `tsc` has to refuse the arithmetic and the dereference `nish` refuses,
and it has to refuse assigning any other value to one. The brand is what makes
it nominal, so a `{}` does not satisfy it; the name is never written, so the
declaration costs a reader nothing.

```ts
interface CPtr
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `readonly __nishForeignPointer: unique symbol` |  |

## ResultMethods

```ts
interface ResultMethods<T, E>
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `expect(message: string): T` | The success payload, or `message` on stderr and exit 1. |
| `isErr(): this is ResultErr<E> & ResultMethods<T, E>` | True when this is the failure arm; narrows `r` the other way. |
| `isOk(): this is ResultOk<T> & ResultMethods<T, E>` | True when this is the success arm; narrows `r` where it is a condition. |
| `orReturn(): T` | The success payload, or an early `return Err(error)` from the enclosing function — Rust's `?`. `nish` additionally requires that function to return a `Result` whose error arm accepts `E`; `tsc` cannot check that. |
| `unwrapOr(fallback: T): T` | The success payload, or `fallback` when this is the failure arm. |

## i32

Ambient declarations for the Nish global surface.

Every Nish program is legal TypeScript syntax — the compiler parses it
with the official TypeScript parser and nothing else. This file is what
makes it legal TypeScript *semantics* too: reference it from a `tsconfig.json`
(or with `/// <reference path="..." />`) and `tsc --noEmit`, your editor and
your language server all accept `Result<T, E>`, `Ok(...)`, `i32` and the rest
without a red squiggle.

  { "include": ["src/**/*.ts", "node_modules/nish/runtime/nish.d.ts"] }

**`nish` is still the authority.** TypeScript's structural checker is
weaker than this compiler's in the places where Nish is deliberately
stricter, and it cannot see the flow rules at all:

  - the integer and float widths are aliases of `number` here, so `tsc`
    lets an `i32` and an `f64` mix where `nish` refuses;
  - `tsc` does not know that a `Result` may not be dropped, that
    `orReturn()` returns early, or that the enclosing function has to
    return a `Result` of its own for it to be legal at all;
  - everything Phase 0 forbids (`any`, `throw`, `try`, prototypes,
    arrow functions, ...) is ordinary TypeScript and passes `tsc` happily.

So a program that `tsc` accepts may still be rejected by `nish`; the
reverse should never happen, and a case where it does is a bug in this file.
`docs/LANGUAGE.md` is the normative description.

**`Map` and `Set` are not declared here**, although `nish` has them as
globals: the `"lib": ["ES2022"]` a program is checked against already
declares JavaScript's, and a second declaration would clash with it.
`nish`'s are that surface less what it defers — no `entries`, no `forEach`,
no `for...of` over a `Map` itself — with `keys()` and `values()` admitted
only as the iterable of a `for...of`, and `get`'s `V | undefined` only as a
`const`'s initialiser, the left of `??` or an operand of `=== undefined`,
none of which `tsc` can know (docs/LANGUAGE.md -> `Map` and `Set`).
`nish/map`'s `reserve` and `getOrInsert` are not declared here either: they
are ordinary source, `std/map.ts`, which `tsconfig.json` maps `nish/*` to.

```ts
type i32 = number
```

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="NET_SO_KEEPALIVE" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`NET_SO_KEEPALIVE: i32`

`SO_KEEPALIVE`: `value` 1 probes an idle connection, 0 does not.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="NET_SO_RCVBUF" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`NET_SO_RCVBUF: i32`

`SO_RCVBUF`: the receive buffer, `value` in bytes; Linux doubles the value it stores.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="NET_SO_SNDBUF" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`NET_SO_SNDBUF: i32`

`SO_SNDBUF`: the send buffer, `value` in bytes; Linux doubles the value it stores.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="NET_TCP_NODELAY" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`NET_TCP_NODELAY: i32`

`TCP_NODELAY`: `value` 1 sends a small write at once, 0 lets Nagle batch it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="NET_TCP_QUICKACK" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`NET_TCP_QUICKACK: i32`

`TCP_QUICKACK` (Linux; -95 elsewhere): `value` 1 acknowledges at once, 0
delays. Linux does not keep quick-ACK mode: the kernel leaves it on its own,
so a server that wants a mode sets it again after every response.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="NET_UNIX_SEQPACKET" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`NET_UNIX_SEQPACKET: i32`

`unixSocketPair` kind: each write one message (`SOCK_SEQPACKET`).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="NET_UNIX_STREAM" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`NET_UNIX_STREAM: i32`

`unixSocketPair` kind: a byte stream.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="NET_UNIX_UNLINK_STALE" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`NET_UNIX_UNLINK_STALE: i32`

`unixListen` flag: unlink a socket file nothing listens on, then bind.

</scalar-card>

`console: Console`
